method.value: Slice cubes into 5" wide pV slices along PA=55 deg with 50% overlap; disk mask = model velocity +- Dv(x); non-disk is the complement

evidence.quote: each slice is $5.0\ensuremath{''}$ (85 pc) wide, and we overlap slices by half their width ($2.5\ensuremath{''}$, 42 pc)

key_parameters.value: Dv(x)=120 exp(-(x/2.5)^2)+100 km/s, x in arcsec

evidence.quote: \Delta v\,(x) = 120\,\exp \left( - \left(\frac{x}{2.5}\right)^2 \right) + 100
the parameters (120, 2.5 and 100) in equation [\[equation: delta v\]](#equation: delta v) are visually selected to fit the fit pV diagrams as best as possible

analysis_steps.goal: Measure CO luminosities and gas masses

method.value: Integrate disk/non-disk luminosity; convert with starburst X_CO and line ratios; split non-disk into outflow, superbubble and other-disk

evidence.quote: The total gas mass $M$ is estimated from the CO line luminosity, using the conversion factor $\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{CO}} = 0.5\times10^{20}
The masses we report include the contribution of Helium to the total mass.
we do not measure line ratios from the images but adopt a uniform factor

validation.value: Masses from the three transitions agree within 10% (disk) and 50% (non-disk); compared with literature masses

evidence.quote: They match within 10% for the disk component, and within 50% for the non-disk component.

analysis_steps.goal: Derive outflow rate, energy and momentum

method.value: Per-voxel rate m/(ds/v), binned by ejection time or distance; deprojected by cone geometry; E=0.5 m v^2, P=m v

evidence.quote: we calculate the outflow rate $\dot{m}_i$ of the gas that was ejected at time $t_{{\mathrm{eject}},i}$ over the time interval $\Delta t_{\mathrm{cross},i}$

key_parameters.value: Cone opening ~60 deg, axis perpendicular to disk, i=78 deg, theta 48-108 deg

evidence.quote: the range of effective inclination of outflowing gas can be anywhere between $\theta = 48^\circ$ and $\theta = 108^\circ$

assumptions.value: Launch in the disk plane; flow perpendicular to bar plane; constant X_CO; two cases: no acceleration after launch, or constant outflow rate

evidence.quote: we assume that the projected direction of flow is perpendicular the the central plane of the bar and that CO emission traces the mass with a constant conversion factor

fitting.value: Monte Carlo over outflow direction on the cone surface; 16th-84th percentiles
